task1.title: How geothermal energy is used to produce electricity
task1.prompt: The diagram below shows how geothermal energy is used to produce electricity.

chartDesc.title: Geothermal power plant

stages.label: Cold water
stages.detail: Cold water is stored in a container above ground.

stages.label: The injection well
stages.detail: Cold water is pumped down 4.5 km into the geothermal zone containing hot rocks.

stages.label: The production well
stages.detail: Hot water heated in the geothermal zone is pumped up towards the surface.

stages.label: Condenser
stages.detail: Hot water passes through the condenser to produce steam.

stages.label: Turbine and Generator
stages.detail: Steam powers the turbine, which drives the generator to produce electricity.

chartDesc.overview: The process consists of 5 main stages, starting with cold water pumped 4.5 km underground to be heated by hot rocks, and finishing with electricity production via a turbine and generator.
keyFeatures: Sequential linear process spanning underground and above-ground stages.
Water is pumped down 4.5 km to the geothermal zone (hot rocks) via an injection well and retrieved via a production well.
Produced steam powers a turbine, which turns a generator that outputs electricity to power pylons.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Children making their own choices
task2.prompt:
Some people believe that allowing children to make their own choices on everyday matters (such as food, clothes and entertainment) is likely to result in a society of individuals who only think about their own wishes. Other people believe that it is important for children to make decisions about matters that affect them.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
